messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] High tail latency + 502s observed across hosted inference gateway. Source: kv-cache pressure on paged block manager. Auto-alert triggered by latency-slo-monitor.
Maya: taking this as oncall. seeing a bunch of 502 + 524 for long requests, spike started ~10m ago. telemetry: KV cache total bytes jumped ~6x on gpu-pool-3, and block-manager logs show frequent full-page reads.
Samir: I deployed a batcher tuning change to reduce cold-starts an hour ago (batch_window_ms: 200 -> 250ms, continuous_batching.max_size bumped). Could be related.
Alex: I can confirm: perf dashboard shows large increase in average batch sizes and many stalled requests waiting on KV fetches. KV cache eviction rates dropped to near zero.
Jordan: customer impact: multiple production customers (including AcmeHealth) report timeouts on long-context requests. Ops reports several 5xx spikes on the public endpoint.
Maya: quick mitigation plan options: 1) revert batch_window_ms to previous value 2) force eviction by lowering block_manager.max_block_bytes 3) enable aggressive metadata sweep to cleanup leaked entries. Which is fastest?
Samir: fastest is revert the batcher config rollback. Reverting will immediately reduce inflight KV entries. I'll push a rollback to canary.
Alex: while Samir rolls back, I can throttle continuous batching on gpu-pool-3 and drain slow KV reads. Command for throttling (do not run on all pools):
```
redwoodctl runtime set-pool-config --pool gpu-pool-3 --key continuous_batching.enabled --value false --env prod
```
Maya: I want both: canary rollback + pool throttle. Also start an eviction spike to free memory proactively.
eng-sre-bot: running: `evict-tool --target gpu-pool-3 --policy size-aware-lru --limit 60%`
Jordan: customer comms: I'll open a thread with affected accounts and share ETA after the first mitigation.
Samir: applied rollback to canary (canary 10% traffic) at revision batcher:v2 -> batcher:v1. Command:
```
redwoodctl rollout rollback --service batcher --from-revision batcher:v2 --to-revision batcher:v1 --percent 10 --env prod
```
Samir: canary metrics: batch sizes down ~40% after 90s, KV cache growth flatlined on canary hosts.
Alex: good. I'm enabling eviction spike on the problematic hosts and reducing block_manager.max_block_bytes to 64MB temporarily (was 256MB). Patch command:
```
redwoodctl config set --component block-manager --key max_block_bytes --value 67108864 --env prod --scope gpu-pool-3
```
Maya: logs from block-manager before eviction:
```
[block-manager] blocks=1200 total_bytes=8700000000 meta_entries=4800 eviction_rate=2/s
[block-manager] last_gc=300s ago, metadata_checks=failed(12), read_latency_avg=85ms
```
Maya: after eviction call:
```
[block-manager] triggered_eviction count=600 freed_bytes=5.2GB eviction_policy=size-aware-lru
[block-manager] total_bytes=3.5GB blocks=520 meta_entries=1800
```
Jordan: initial customer updates posted. AcmeHealth reported partial recovery but still seeing occasional tails.
Samir: rolling the rollback to 50% now. Will monitor KV cache size and tail latency.
Alex: also found a metadata leak path in the block manager: metadata entries for evicted blocks weren't being cleaned for some rare error path when block digest mismatch occurs. PR with fix: PR#4823. Hotpatch plan: backport to current prod release and deploy to block-manager nodes on gpu-pool-3 first.
Maya: escalate to Sev-2. Not Sev-1 since traffic is degraded but most requests succeed eventually. Noting SLA potential for some customers.
Samir: applying hotpatch to canary block-manager hosts (rolling restart). Command:
```
redwoodctl deploy --service block-manager --image redwood/block-manager:prod-hotfix-4823 --env prod --scope gpu-pool-3 --strategy rolling
```
eng-sre-bot: patch deployed to canary nodes (2 nodes). Observing metadata GC success on canary: "metadata_sweep: removed 2.2k orphan entries".
Alex: metrics post-hotpatch on canary: KV cache bytes down to ~2.8GB, eviction_rate normalized, read_latency tail decreased from 160ms -> 48ms.
Maya: Samir, once canary looks stable for 5min, roll to remaining pool nodes. Jordan, keep customer comm loop updated: ETA for full mitigation ~20-30m.
Jordan: posted update to affected customers: engineers applied rollback and are deploying a block-manager hotfix; expected reduced errors in 30m. I'll tag support and account teams.
Samir: rolling to 100% now. Monitor: latency SLO by model and by region. If any spike we can toggle continuous_batching.enabled false globally as emergency kill-switch.
Maya: oncall handoff: I'll stay for another 15m, then handoff to Samir for post-rollout monitoring. Samir, call me if any regression.
Samir: copied. I'll keep monitoring dashboards and watch KV metrics: total_bytes, blocks, meta_entries, eviction_rate, batch_size.
Alex: follow-up remediation actions (post-incident):
- revert batcher change fully and run canary load tests
- add safety limit to continuous batching (max_inflight_entries per pool)
- add automated eviction trigger when total_bytes > threshold
- backport PR#4823 and add unit tests for metadata cleanup path
- instrument more metrics for block manager metadata churn
Maya: log incident timeline and tag as "paged-kv-blockmanager-metadata-leak". Assign postmortem to Alex + Samir. Severity: Sev-2. Impact: increased 5xx and tail-latency for hosted customers; partial customer timeouts for long-context requests.
eng-sre-bot: Incident declared: Sev-2. Incident channel pinned. Playbook runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/paged-kv-incident
Jordan: I'll keep customer channel active and coordinate follow-ups. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
